items.quote: We used the very high temperature calorimeter which has been employed in previous investigations. This apparatus can work at temperature up to 1800 K and has been already described in detail. 48 The two laboratory and reference crucibles are superimposed along a vertical axis and each of them is encircled by the 25 solders of (Pt + Rh6 pct in mass/Pt + Rh 30 pct in mass) thermocouples constituting the sensing device. All this arrangement is located into a gas-tight alumina tube and surrounded by the graphite resistor of a furnace which can be linearly temperature programmed. The metallic alloy under investigation is contained in the upper crucible while the second crucible is filled with an inert material (pure alumina). The preparation of the samples depends on the nature of the investigated alloy. All the samples of Ag + Au + Ge alloys were previously synthesized. Stoichiometric amounts of gold, silver, and germanium were introduced into a quartz cell and sealed under purified argon atmosphere. The total mass of each sample was about 500 mg. These alloys were prepared and homogenized in the liquid state into a separate furnace during many heating-cooling cycles; then they were introduced into the laboratory crucible for thermal analysis. All the thermal effects arising on h e a t i n g - - o r cooli n g - d u r i n g the successive phase equilibria in the ternary alloy were detected by the 25 thermocouples and the temperatures by a single thermocouple (Pt/Pt + Rh 10 pct in mass), the solder of which is located in the upper part of the laboratory crucible. The heating rate varied between 2 and 5 K 9 mn -]. On the temperature range (800 K to 1400 K) the mean uncertainty of temperature measurements is about --+3 K.

The principle of this apparatus is identical with that of the Calvet microcalorimeter. Each cylindrical cell--laboratory and refere n c e - - i s surrounded by a thermal fluxmeter and located into a metallic block, the temperature of which can be linearly programmed. The cell is a gas-tight silica (or Pyrex or stainless steel) tube 6 mm in diameter and 20 mm in length. The heating (or cooling) rate varies from 2 K. mn-1 to 4 K. mn -].
